questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. You may need to move from the outside of the curve to the inside before straightening out.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.explanation: Flash your brake light if someone is tailgating you. This warns them that you are about to slow down. Also flash your brake light if you are slowing down unexpectedly.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, what is NOT important?

options.text: Designed to meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards, fits snugly, and has no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks is not important.

questions.question: How should you pack a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: The heavier items should go toward the front.
The heavier items should go toward the rear.
Mounting loads behind the rear axle is recommended.
Lighter items should be stored in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The heavier items should go toward the front.
questions.explanation: Put heavier items toward the front of the load. Keep the load over or in front of the rear axle. Pack lighter items behind you.

questions.question: What should you do when braking on a slippery surface?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use abrupt pressure on the front brake to prevent locking the front tire.
Use either brake, but use only one brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes on slippery surfaces. Squeeze the front brake gradually to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Avoid placing you in other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Provide you with an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see better, stay out of blind spots, and gives you an escape route. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed

questions.explanation: Three factors affect BAC: how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Gender, physical condition, and food intake also matter. How often you drink does not.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Should be placed in front of the operator.
Should be placed behind the operator.
Does not have to be able to reach the footrests.
Should hold onto the motorcycle frame.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be placed behind the operator.
questions.explanation: A child should always sit directly behind the operator. A child in front cannot balance properly and may get in the way of the controls.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When the left arm is bent at the elbow with the hand pointing up, it means the rider plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Put inexperienced riders at the back.
Keep enough space between you and other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space between you and other riders.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. Check your mirrors to see riders behind you. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Keep proper space between all riders in the group.

questions.question: Swerving a motorcycle:

options.text: Should be done to avoid hazards on slippery roads.

questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of traction. Do not swerve on slippery surfaces because you may lose control.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before you slow down suddenly. This warns tailgaters who may not see hazards ahead that you are slowing.

questions.question: The right footwear for riding a motorcycle:
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels may catch on things. Tuck in laces so they do not get caught.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle best, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with arms fully stretched out.
Use arms to hold their body up.
Keep knees away from the gas tank.
Keep feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not hold you up. Keep your arms slightly bent on the handgrips. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests to stay balanced.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object on the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as you can before impact. Try to hit the object at a 90-degree angle. Keep the motorcycle upright and rise slightly off the seat. Ease off the throttle slightly before impact.

questions.question: Each traffic lane gives a motorcyclist how many paths of travel?
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane provides three paths for motorcyclists: left, center, and right.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following except:

options.text: Help you set up for turns.
Help you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.
Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. A good position discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle under normal conditions, keep a minimum distance of:
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance behind other vehicles under normal conditions. Increase this distance when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You must finish the pass in a passing zone.
You can finish the pass in a no passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You should make eye contact with the other driver.
You should ride on the shoulder if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: Always complete a pass only in a passing zone. Pass only when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which of these do you NOT need to adjust?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle with a passenger sits differently because of the extra weight. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlights, and mirrors. You do not need to adjust brake light position.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handle grip toward the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip away from the direction you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip toward the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right grip to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left grip.

questions.question: What is the best lane position?

options.text: Always ride on the right side of the lane.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.
Change your position based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position as riding conditions change to stay safe.

questions.question: If you must brake while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are out of the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gently than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans in a curve, the tires have less grip. Always try to straighten the bike before braking. If you must brake in a curve, brake smoothly and gently.

questions.question: How do you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Swerve toward the side with fewer hazards.
Try to accelerate while the brake is still engaged.

questions.explanation: To regain control of a locked rear wheel, release the brake. If you lock the rear brake on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which of these should you NOT tell them to do?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.explanation: Passengers should stay quiet to help you focus on riding. Passengers should board after the engine starts, sit forward without crowding you, and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is following the car ahead too closely.
Someone is sitting in a parked car.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing someone walking in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others before passing. A driver following too close may suddenly cut in front of you. Use your horn when passing a parked car with someone inside or when passing pedestrians or cyclists in the street. Do not use your horn just to get attention.

questions.question: When riding at night, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: At night, use your high beam when safe, use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective clothing. Change your lane position as needed to see better, be seen better, and have space to move.

questions.question: When braking in a curve, what happens?

options.text: It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more grip as you lean into the curve.
You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but it takes great care. When the motorcycle leans in a curve, the tires use some of their grip to turn. This means less grip is available for braking.
